title: a subprocess script that ends normally is in its seal's closure
intention: A python script a proof runs as a subprocess is named in the seal's closure however it exits, so an edit to it stales the seal.
why: Law 8: a seal an edit to its subject cannot expire is a quiet green that peers lean on. A python script a proof runs as a SUBPROCESS is missing from the reach log when it runs to its last line, .py and extensionless alike, so editing it cannot stale the seal. CPython 3.14.4 pops __main__.__file__ once the script completes, and cairn/devices/tester/reach/sitecustomize.py reads every module __file__ at atexit, after the pop. A script that raises SystemExit keeps __file__ and IS logged. Repro, 2026-11-20 on akiendelllinux: /var/tmp/noext_probe = 'import sys,atexit; atexit.register(lambda: print("atexit", getattr(sys.modules["__main__"],"__file__",None)))' then a plain last line prints 'atexit None' (also as noext_probe.py); /var/tmp/noext_probe2 ending 'raise SystemExit(0)' prints 'atexit /var/tmp/noext_probe2'. Live: CAIRN_TESTER_REACH_LOG=<f> PYTHONPATH=cairn/devices/tester/reach python3 cairn/devices/tester/proofs/fixtures/extensionless_leaf (then ending normally) logged only the editable finder and sitecustomize.py. Found building b7d5df9919fe's clause 4; all 28 bin/cmd scripts exit via SystemExit, so the gates are covered and the blind set is any other subprocess-run script that ends normally.
how: In cairn/devices/tester/reach/sitecustomize.py, the atexit logger also records the main script when __main__ no longer carries __file__: sys.argv[0] when it names an existing file (a -c child's argv[0] is '-c' and a -m child's __main__ keeps __file__, so neither invents a path). Capturing at import is not available — sitecustomize runs before __main__ is set. Proof cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_a_subprocess_script_that_ends_normally_is_in_the_seals_closure.py under PROVES this ticket's id, clauses 1-3: a CAIRN_*_FIXTURE env re-run of itself that subprocess-runs a committed normally-ending fixture, sealed through run_proof, closure read. Note the extensionless half also needs b7d5df9919fe's repo_relative_closure edit; build after it lands.

clauses.claim: a fixture proof that runs a repo .py script as a subprocess (sys.executable <script>), the script ending by falling off its last line, sealed through TesterDevice().run_proof, names that script in its fingerprint_closure, and the script's bytes move sealed_fingerprint_now
the same holds for an EXTENSIONLESS script ending normally (cairn/devices/tester/proofs/fixtures/extensionless_leaf's shape, without its SystemExit)

no invented path: a `python -c` child and a `python -m <module>` child add nothing to the closure that the run did not execute, and cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_a_seal_records_what_it_reached.py stays green

decisions.text: D1: the reach logger records sys.argv[0] as the main script when __main__ has lost __file__ and argv[0] is a file.
D2: the proof plus validation and two committed normally-ending fixtures (a .py and an extensionless one, clause 2's), one tooth per clause.

measured.saw: under the reach sitecustomize at origin/main 887096c2b, CPython 3.14.4: a script of print(1) alone logged no script path; with raise SystemExit(0) or sys.exit(0) it logged its own path; a -c child's argv[0] is '-c' and __main__ has no __file__; a -m child (python -m mm) logged mm.py. sys.argv is already set when sitecustomize loads (argv[0] the script as typed, cwd unchanged), so D1 resolves argv[0] at load and adds it at exit only when __main__ lost __file__
